title: Policy evaluation on the 4×4 gridworld
summary: Evaluating the equiprobable random policy on a 4×4 grid with reward −1 per move. The value function converges to the negated expected number of steps to the terminal corner; the greedy policy with respect to the estimates is already optimal from the third sweep.

facts.claim: The printed v_k for k = 1, 2, 3 and 10 are the two-array iterates of (4.5), shown to one decimal.
The k = ∞ grid is v_π, whose values are the integers −14, −18, −20 and −22.
v_π satisfies the Bellman equation (4.4) at every state.
The greedy policies from the third iteration on are optimal (they equal the greedy policy for v_π).
The in-place algorithm of Figure 4.1 converges to the same v_π, in fewer sweeps than the two-array version.

verification.note: Every cell of Figure 4.2 was transcribed from the page image and compared.

flags.note: Figure 4.2 prints values to one decimal with an unusual tie rule: −2.875 appears as −2.9 and −8.352 as −8.4 (so not truncation), but the exact value −1.75 at k = 2 appears as −1.7. The only simple rule matching every cell is 'nearest, exact halves toward zero'. The values themselves are correct; only the display rounding is unusual.
